_readme: All the words of The Pitch live here. Change any sentence between quotes and keep the quotes, commas and brackets as they are. 'roast' is Alice at level 5, 'soft' is the gentle setting, 'clean' is the no-swearing version. Where a line has an 'fr' part, that is the French translation shown underneath during the first steps. 'celebrations' are the punchy lines Alice shouts, one at random, every time the learner gets it right. Each lesson in 'lessons' follows the 5 steps: hook, three phrases, your turn (replies: good true/false), feedback (fix, brilliant, traps) and send-off. 'situation' is the room it belongs to.

welcome.roast: I'm Alice. I've sat through a thousand meetings so you don't have to suffer through one more in silence. Ready?
welcome.soft: I'm Alice. I'll help you speak up in English meetings, one small step at a time.

fr.roast: Moi, c'est Alice. J'ai survécu à mille réunions pour que vous n'en subissiez plus une seule en silence. Prêt·e ?
fr.soft: Moi, c'est Alice. Je vais vous aider à prendre la parole en réunion en anglais, petit à petit.

comeback.roast: When the shit hits the fan, some guys run and some guys stay… glad you decided to stay.
comeback.clean: When things get tough, some people run and some people stay… glad you decided to stay.
comeback.soft: Welcome back! Lovely to see you. Shall we do five minutes?

meeting.roast: You apologised three times in one sentence last week. You're not British, you don't get the discount.
meeting.soft: Breathe, smile, and remember: they want to hear what you think.

settings.roast: Turn me down if you must. I'll still be thinking it.
settings.soft: No problem, I'll be gentle. Mostly.

voiceCheckReplies.roast: Your shoes aren't going to pitch for you, darling. We start with Survive. Lots of it.
voiceCheckReplies.soft: Totally normal. We'll start with ready-made phrases that get you through.

fr.roast: Vos chaussures ne vont pas pitcher à votre place, chéri·e. On commence par Survive. Beaucoup de Survive.
fr.soft: C'est tout à fait normal. On commence par des phrases toutes prêtes pour vous en sortir.

voiceCheckReplies.roast: Translating in your head again? I can hear the gears from here. We'll speed you up.
voiceCheckReplies.soft: You understand more than you think. Let's get you speaking sooner.

fr.roast: Encore en train de traduire dans votre tête ? J'entends les rouages d'ici. On va accélérer tout ça.
fr.soft: Vous comprenez plus que vous ne le pensez. On va vous faire parler plus tôt.

voiceCheckReplies.roast: So you're fluent, just… beige. Let's give you some personality in English.
voiceCheckReplies.soft: Great base. Now let's make your English sound like you.

fr.roast: Donc vous parlez anglais, mais… en beige. On va donner un peu de personnalité à votre anglais.
fr.soft: Belle base. Maintenant, faisons en sorte que votre anglais vous ressemble.

situations: Ask for budget, time or help
Write an email that gets a reply

ask: Frame it so the answer is yes
nego: Hold your number with a smile
chair: Keep it on time, bring quiet people in
network: Make a contact who calls you back

phraseBank: Nice to meet you, I'm in charge of…
Sorry, could you say that again?
Let me get back to you on that.

phrases: I see where you're coming from, but the results speak for themselves.
Let me explain why this matters for the team.
Could we look at what we'd lose if we cut it?

attack.brad: Honestly? Nobody needs this. Let's cut it and move on.
attack.boss: Hmm. I'm not sure. Maybe. Let's see. What do you think, quickly?

replies: bad
OK, no problem, we can cut it.
You folded faster than a deckchair. Stand your ground, darling.
Too quick to give up. You can push back politely.
fr
I am not agree, it is very important.
“I am not agree.” The Marseillaise again. It's “I don't agree”.
Nearly! It's “I don't agree”, no “am”.
good
I see where you're coming from, but the results speak for themselves. Let me show you.
Look at you. Brad just sat down and said nothing. A first.
Perfect: calm, clear and convincing.

phrases: I understand, and here's why the number makes sense.
If we can agree on the timing, I can be flexible on the details.
I'd rather find something that works for both of us.

attack.brad: That's way too much. Give me twenty percent off or we're done.
attack.boss: It feels… expensive? Can you do something? Whatever you think.

replies: bad
Sorry, sorry, OK, twenty percent.
You just gave away twenty percent and an apology. Hold your number with a smile.
Don't give in straight away. Hold your number.
fr
I can make an effort on the price, it is possible.
“Make an effort” is very French. In English: “I can be flexible on…”.
Try “I can be flexible on…” instead.
good
I understand. If we can agree on the timing, I can be flexible on the details.
Oh, that's a negotiator. Brad is now Googling you.
Excellent. You stayed firm and friendly.

phrases: I'll keep this short: three points.
The key thing to remember is this.
Happy to take questions at the end.

attack.brad: Can you just get to the point? I've got another call in five.
attack.boss: So… what's the… you know, the main thing? In one sentence?

replies: bad
Euh, yes, sorry, so, euh, I will explain everything…
That “euh” lasted longer than my last relationship. Breathe, then speak.
Take a breath before you start. Fewer “euh”.
fr
Actually, I will present you the planning.
“Actually” means “en fait”, not “actuellement”. And it's “the schedule”.
Careful: “actually” means “en fait”. And say “the schedule”.
good
Of course. Three points, two minutes. The key thing is this:
Short, sharp, in control. Brad's other call can wait.
Great: short, clear and confident.

lessons.title: Disagree politely

hook.roast: Saying “No, that's wrong” in a meeting is how you get fewer meetings. Let's fix that.
hook.soft: Saying “No, that's wrong” can sound harsh in English. Let's find a smoother way.

lessons.hookFr: Aujourd'hui : être en désaccord sans claquer la porte.

phrases.say: I see where you're coming from, but…
phrases.fr: Je comprends votre point de vue, mais…

phrases.say: I'm not sure that's the best option.
phrases.fr: Je ne suis pas sûr·e que ce soit la meilleure option.

phrases.html: Could we look at it from another angle?
phrases.say: Could we look at it from another angle?
phrases.fr: Et si on regardait ça sous un autre angle ?

lessons.tip: Le piège français : on dit I agree, jamais « I am agree ».

character.name: Brad · New York
character.line: Let's just cut the training budget. Nobody uses it anyway.

replies.roast: Brilliant. Brad now hates you and the budget is still cut. Softer, darling. Try again.
replies.soft: A bit direct for a meeting. Try a softer way in.
replies.fix: Soften before you push back: “I see where you're coming from, but…”

replies.text: I am not agree with you.
replies.roast: “I am not agree.” The whole meeting just heard the Marseillaise. It's “I don't agree”. Again.
replies.soft: Nearly! In English it's “I don't agree”, no “am”. Try again.
replies.fix: It's “I don't agree”, never “I am not agree”.

replies.text: I see where you're coming from, but the numbers tell a different story.
replies.roast: Oh, look at you. That sentence would get you a second meeting and someone else's parking space.

lessons.noFix: Nothing to fix. Annoying, frankly. Next time, add a reason: “…because the numbers show…”
lessons.brilliant: Your stress on “but” was perfect. Brad felt that.
lessons.endTitle: You just disagreed with someone in English and nobody died.

sendoff.roast: Same time tomorrow? I'll bring the coffee. You bring the confidence.

newPhrases: I see where you're coming from, but…
I'm not sure that's the best option.
Could we look at it from another angle?

lessons.title: Move a meeting

hook.roast: Ask an English colleague to “advance the meeting” and they'll think you want to promote it. Today we move meetings like a pro.
hook.soft: Today: how to move a meeting in English, without the false friends.

lessons.hookFr: Aujourd'hui : avancer, reporter ou déplacer une réunion, sans faux amis.

phrases.html: Could we bring the meeting forward to Tuesday?
phrases.say: Could we bring the meeting forward to Tuesday?

phrases.html: Would it be OK to push it back to three o'clock?
phrases.say: Would it be OK to push it back to three o'clock?

phrases.html: Shall we move it to the main meeting room instead?
phrases.say: Shall we move it to the main meeting room instead?
phrases.fr: Changer de salle (ou : « switch to Teams »)

lessons.tip: Pour finir, vérifiez toujours : Does that still work for you?

character.name: Brad · New York
character.line: Hey, bad news. I'm stuck in Lyon. I have to stay here until Thursday, so we need to move Tuesday's meeting.

replies.text: Oh no! So you rest in Lyon until Thursday?
replies.roast: “Rest”? Brad isn't having a nap in Lyon, darling. Rester is stay. To rest is se reposer. Brad has to stay.
replies.soft: Careful: “rester” is “to stay”. “To rest” means “se reposer”.
replies.fix: Rester = to stay. To rest = se reposer.

replies.text: No problem, we can retard the meeting to Thursday.
replies.roast: “Retard” is an insult in English, darling. Brad is now on the phone to HR. It's “push back”.
replies.clean: “Retard” is a very rude word in English. Brad's eyebrows just hit the ceiling. It's “push back”.
replies.soft: Avoid “retard”: it's offensive in English. Say “push back”.

replies.text: Can we advance it to Monday?
replies.roast: “Advance” it? It's a meeting, not a soldier. It's “bring forward”. Also, Brad has to stay in Lyon until Thursday. Keep up.
replies.soft: Avancer = “bring forward”. And Brad can't come before Thursday.

replies.text: No problem. Shall we push it back to Thursday at ten, and do it on Teams in case you're running late?
replies.roast: New time, new venue, one sentence. Brad's assistant wants your number.
replies.soft: Perfect: new time, new place, clear and friendly.

lessons.noFix: Nothing to fix. Show-off. Next time, finish with “Does that still work for you?”
lessons.brilliant: New time and new venue in one sentence. That's how you run a call.
lessons.endTitle: You just moved a meeting without moving a muscle in your face.

sendoff.roast: Same time tomorrow? Or shall we push it back?

newPhrases: Could we bring the meeting forward to Tuesday?
Would it be OK to push it back to three o'clock?
Shall we move it to the main meeting room instead?
I have to stay until Thursday.
Does that still work for you?
